Case study 01 — Enterprise SaaS

SalesVision Director Portal

A boardroom-grade sales-ops portal, designed so a Director knows within five seconds whether anything needs their attention today.

Outcome 12 screens specified, 4 of them screens the live build didn't have, and 5 documented spec conflicts closed — delivered as design system v1.1 plus a working prototype.
Product
SalesVision (CRM Vision)
Role
Sole designer — system + 12 screens
Scope
Director role, desktop-first 1440px
Deliverable
Design system v1.1 + built prototype
sec 02
The problem

Three source documents described three different products. The PRD said the Director was strictly read-only across seven screens. The live build let Directors create departments, teams and managers — across four analytics tabs, with no lead board and no reports centre. And the functional spec flagged its own UX debt: every screen kept its own independent time filter.

Nobody had reconciled them. So the first deliverable wasn't a screen — it was a decision table.

reconciliation.md — 5 conflicts resolved
READ-ONLYAnalytics stays read-only + export. Org creation survives, gated behind an explicit can_manage_org capability.
SCREENSBuild both sets. The PRD's Lead Board and MIS Centre are real gaps — added, not dropped.
FILTEROne persistent global period, read by every screen. The single biggest structural fix.
EXPORTXLSX + PDF with a download history log — closes the PRD's own audit requirement.
DRILL-INYou could drill into a lead but never into a rep. Added an Executive Profile screen.
sec 03
The reversal

v1.0 invented a palette. v1.1 threw it away.

v1.0 used the Material Dashboard reference for layout and behaviour only, then invented its own indigo-blue accent and dark-navy sidebar. The feedback was blunt: replicate the reference literally. So I re-skinned the entire system — near-black as the only functional UI colour, a white sidebar, colour reserved for data alone — and left the structure, screen architecture and data model untouched. A re-skin, not a re-plan.

v1.0 — invented killed

Indigo accent, dark-navy gradient sidebar, per-module colour coding. Reads like every other dashboard template.

v1.1 — shipped shipped

#17181C is the only functional colour — buttons, active nav, KPI icon squares. Green and red belong to the data.

KPI anatomy

Label, value, signed delta stacked left; a 44px black icon square top-right. Never a left accent bar, never module-coloured. Numbers roll up from zero on load.

Colour discipline

Every button and active nav state is black. Green, slate and red exist only inside charts, deltas and status pills — so colour always means something.

Nothing is a dead end

Every row that names a person routes to their Executive Profile; every lead card to Lead Detail. The table is a navigation surface, not a readout.

sec 05
Live prototype

Click through it yourself.

The real shell, wired: sidebar navigation, the global period filter every screen reads from, and the Executives / Managers toggle. Unbuilt screens return the placeholder they were specified to return.

salesvisionai.com/director — live, interactive Interactive
One period filter

Switch the period and every number above it moves. No screen in the system owns its own date filter — a rule set in Step 1 so twelve screens could never drift apart.

Nothing is a dead end

Every nav item routes somewhere from day one. Screens that weren't built yet return a labelled placeholder rather than a broken click — the wiring was the deliverable.

Same shell, three answers

Dashboard, Mapping and Leads share one chrome and one colour rule. Black is structure; green, slate and red only ever appear inside data.

OUTCOME SHEET
Proof
What shipped

Twelve screens, one state machine, zero dead ends.

12
Screens specified
4
New screens the build lacked
5
Spec conflicts resolved
1
Global filter, finally
Bugs the design fixed

A transparent modal backdrop, filter state lost on scroll, no confirm-before-discard, no success toast, and hand-rolled skeletons per tab — all flagged in the functional spec, all specified out in v1.1.

What I'd do differently

I designed the whole Director portal before a single Director used it. The reconciliation table was the right instinct; validating it with two real Directors before locking twelve screens would have been better.
